claim: Progressive resistance training improves multiple physical-capacity outcomes in healthy adults, while the most useful prescription variables depend on the target outcome.
population: healthy adults represented across 137 systematic reviews
comparator: non-training or alternative resistance-training prescriptions, depending on the underlying review
outcome: strength, hypertrophy, power, muscular endurance, balance, gait speed, and physical function
study_design: overview of systematic reviews supporting an ACSM position stand
effect_direction: beneficial overall; prescription-variable effects vary by outcome
uncertainty: This umbrella-level claim does not establish an individual athlete's optimal exercise, dose, load, or progression rule.
limitations: The source synthesizes heterogeneous reviews and populations.
The claim intentionally omits precise effects and subgroup rules not represented in this seed.
applicability_notes: Relevant to general healthy-adult resistance training; individual safety, experience, goals, and environment still govern application.

claim: Concurrent aerobic and strength training did not compromise maximal strength or whole-muscle hypertrophy overall, but explosive-strength adaptation may be attenuated when both modes occur in the same session.
outcome: maximal strength, muscle hypertrophy, and explosive strength
effect_direction: mostly neutral for maximal strength and whole-muscle hypertrophy; possible attenuation for explosive strength
uncertainty: Findings are group averages and do not establish a universal scheduling rule for every athlete or modality combination.
limitations: Subgroup results depend on training sequencing and study characteristics.
This seed does not encode an interference coefficient or recovery interval.
applicability_notes: Useful when reviewing mixed-mode plans, but insufficient by itself to prescribe session ordering or spacing.

claim: Some physical adaptations can be maintained for a period with reduced training frequency or volume when training intensity is maintained, but the evidence and minimum dose vary by outcome and population.
population: general and tactical populations summarized in the narrative review
intervention: reduced training frequency or volume with maintained intensity
outcome: maintenance of endurance, strength, and muscle size
duration: short- to medium-term periods represented in the reviewed literature
effect_direction: maintenance may be possible with reduced dose in some contexts
uncertainty: The review does not justify one universal minimum dose, and evidence is limited for some populations and outcomes.
limitations: Narrative rather than systematic review methods.
Population- and adaptation-specific evidence gaps remain.
No operational maintenance threshold is seeded from this claim.
applicability_notes: Supports treating maintenance as a distinct planning state, not selecting an athlete-specific dose without further evidence.
